lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A cross between a bear and an owl that hugs like a bear and attacks with its beak; Baldur's Gate 3 lists owlbears among its Forgotten Realms monsters.

from.quote: An owlbear is depicted as a cross between a bear and an owl, which "hugs" like a bear and attacks with its beak.
The game features monsters from the Forgotten Realms, including owlbears, gnolls, and mind flayers.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: In the tabletop lore an owlbear is a meat-eater with a fierce temper. A mated pair shares a cave, and it will go after anything larger than a mouse.

from.quote: owlbears are carnivorous creatures, famed for their aggression and ferocity; they live in mated pairs in caves and hunt any creature bigger than a mouse.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A race of warriors, almost always evil, who attack the mind flayer ship at the start of the game riding red dragons.

from.quote: the ship comes under attack from githyanki warriors riding red dragons
Alignment || Almost always any evil

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: They are after a companion's prism. Tabletop lore calls them ancient enemies of the githzerai, and says they began as the slave army that rose against the mind flayers.

from.quote: Shadowheart's mysterious prism, a device that is sought after by the githyanki
Of the ten companions, six can be chosen as the player character in the character creator.
Shadowheart is a half-human, half-high elf cleric of Shar
They are cousins and ancient enemies to the githzerai.
The illithid empire was shattered by the slave rebellion

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A drow paladin who leads a band of goblins and other creatures for the game's antagonist in the first act and clashes with the Emerald Grove refugee settlement.

from.quote: Race || Drow
Class || Paladin
she leads a band of goblins and other creatures in service of the game's antagonist
This brings her into conflict with a refugee settlement called the Emerald Grove

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: You can join her raid on the grove, fight her and kill her along with her goblins, or skip the raid and spare her: either knock her out with non-lethal damage while you kill her commanders, or simply leave her alone.

from.quote: the player may either help her raid it or oppose and kill her and her goblins
the player may avoid the raid entirely and keep her alive by either knocking her out with non-lethal damage while killing her commanders or ignoring her entirely

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: If you skip the raid and spare her, the grove is lost.

from.quote: though this option will cause the grove to be slaughtered off-screen

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: Goblins are evil humanoids, a common and weaker monster kind in the tabletop game. In the first act a goblin horde that worships a cult of the Absolute is up against the druids and the tiefling refugees at the Emerald Grove.

from.quote: goblins are a common and fairly weak race of evil humanoid monsters
local druids and tiefling refugees face off against the goblin horde that worships a cult of the "Absolute"

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: The first-edition tabletop monster book describes goblins as a tribal society in dismal surroundings, and low-level characters often face them. The first act's locations include a goblin camp, and Minthara leads a band of goblins in that act.

from.quote: The goblin appears in the first edition Monster Manual (1977), where it is described as having a tribal society and dwelling in dismal surroundings.
from.quote_at: Publication history > Advanced Dungeons & Dragons 1st edition (1977–1988)

from.quote: Goblins are non-human monsters that low-level player characters often face in combat.
Players have access to several locations, including a druids' grove, goblin camp, and a monastery
she leads a band of goblins and other creatures in service of the game's antagonist

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: A barrel that counts as an item you can store in your camp stash and as an environmental element you can exploit in combat.

from.quote: Environmental elements like explosive barrels can be exploited
Items, like explosive barrels, can be sent to a camp stash and retrieved later.

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: In a fight, explosive barrels are part of the surroundings you can turn to your advantage.

from.quote: Environmental elements like explosive barrels can be exploited

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: You can send a barrel to your camp stash and take it out again later.

from.quote: Items, like explosive barrels, can be sent to a camp stash and retrieved later.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: Drinkable items, including health potions and one that lets you talk to animals.

from.quote: Using a spell or potion, players can speak to any encountered animal
as if they are a health potion

lines.label: Uses
lines.text: Drinking a potion consumes a bonus action; attacking with a sword or casting a spell consumes an action.

from.quote: Major instructions to a character, like attacking with a sword or casting a spell, consume an action. Smaller commands, like jumping or drinking a potion, consume a bonus action.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: Actions, bonus actions and movement are separate turn resources, so a potion does not cost you your attack or spell.

from.quote: The primary resources are actions, bonus actions, and movement.
Major instructions to a character, like attacking with a sword or casting a spell, consume an action. Smaller commands, like jumping or drinking a potion, consume a bonus action.

lines.label: Summary
lines.text: Poison that weapons can be dipped in, one of the combat options the game lists beside exploiting explosive barrels.

from.quote: Environmental elements like explosive barrels can be exploited, and weapons can be dipped in poison.

lines.label: Tips
lines.text: You apply it by using the poison item itself, much as you would use a health potion. Polygon's reviewer thought that was unintuitive.

from.quote: Polygon's Maddy Myers criticised some elements as unintuitive, citing how weapons are dipped in poison by interacting with them as if they are a health potion instead of the "dip weapon" function
